meaning: The number 328 appears in the Bible as the count of descendants of Hashum (Nehemiah 7:22), and corresponds in Jewish gematria to the Hebrew word "חשך" (choshekh) – "darkness".
description: In Nehemiah 7:22, the descendants of Hashum are listed as numbering 328, part of the register of those who returned from the Babylonian exile. This count highlights God’s faithfulness in preserving His people through the darkness of exile and bringing them back to the land of promise. In Jewish gematria tradition, 328 corresponds to the Hebrew word "חשך" (choshekh), meaning "darkness." The word appears already in Genesis 1:2, where darkness covers the deep before God creates light. Darkness carries rich symbolic meaning in the Bible, representing both the absence of divine light, chaos and the unknown, but also God’s hidden presence—a theme that reflects the exile experience endured by the returning families.

footnotes.text: In Ezra 2:19, the descendants of Hashum are listed as 223, which differs from the number 328 in Nehemiah 7:22. Such differences between the two lists may be due to different times of registration or different criteria for who was included.

The Hebrew word "חשך" (choshekh) has a gematria value of 328 (ח=8, ש=300, כ=20). The word appears over 100 times in the Hebrew Bible and ranges from the primordial darkness in the creation account to the darkness as the ninth plague in Egypt (Exodus 10:21–23).

In Kabbalistic tradition, darkness is not understood exclusively as something negative, but as a stage of concealment (hester panim) that must be passed through before spiritual enlightenment. Darkness is seen as part of the divine process in which light ultimately shines more brightly.
